static_traits.name: Chen Kai
static_traits.social_status: Has a few colleagues to talk to, but hard to discuss personal feelings
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems in the past; has not yet received psychotherapy or counseling; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, candid tone; self-reported anxiety but hopeful

basic_info.main_problem: Believing oneself unworthy of entering intimate relationships because of divorce, leading to a low sense of self-worth and loneliness, and further avoiding socializing, fearing being rejected.
basic_info.core_demands: 'Loneliness and negative self-perception have become hard to bear, affecting daily life and emotional health, prompting me to seek counseling.' Hoping to 'get rid of these negative thoughts and start feeling better about myself'.
growth_experiences: The 'self-unworthiness' and loneliness that began after the divorce two years ago and gradually worsened: attributing the divorce to personal failure, believing oneself not good enough; experiencing strong feelings of failure and loneliness when seeing happy couples or trying to socialize; tending to avoid socializing and channel energy into work and hobbies to cope with these feelings, yet the emotions persist; this problem affects work performance in the emergency room, interpersonal trust and relationship building, and further disrupts sleep and overall physical and mental health; although there are a few colleagues to talk with, it is hard to discuss private feelings.

core_beliefs: I am unworthy of having intimate relationships
I am a failure (divorce proves I am not good enough)

special_situations.event: Seeing a couple laughing in a cafe
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If divorced, one is destined to never again have a happy intimate relationship
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding social situations, instead channeling energy into work and hobbies
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never again have that kind of happiness

special_situations.event: Trying to meet new people or attending social activities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others know I am divorced, they will judge or reject me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Withdrawing in advance and avoiding contact with strangers
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will look down on me because I am divorced

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One failed marriage means I am generally not good enough and not worthy of being loved
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Interpreting failure through self-blame and self-labeling, while reducing socializing to avoid failing again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Divorce proves I am unworthy of entering relationships

special_situations.event: Comparing others' and one's own relationship status (e.g. seeing happy couples)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as I have no stable relationship, it means I am at a disadvantage, and all other positive evidence is not important
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses on negative cues, ignores colleagues' positive feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as others

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted and loved, to rebuild a stable intimate relationship
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of being judged and rejected, afraid of failing and being hurt again
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being rejected by keeping distance and avoiding socializing
Uses work and hobbies to distract attention and maintain emotional stability

object_relations.self_representation: A failure unworthy of being loved (a divorced person)
object_relations.object_representation: Others/potential partners who will judge and ultimately reject oneself

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor presses 'what evidence supports that others will evaluate you for divorcing'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing people all look down on oneself in their hearts, just not saying it aloud (transference: projecting self-deprecation as others' evaluation)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Adopt a gentle, supportive exploratory tone; acknowledge feelings while guiding toward concrete evidence, inviting distinction between 'feelings' and 'facts'; use open-ended questioning and clarification, pausing appropriately to promote self-awareness.

manifestations: Loneliness worsened two years after the divorce
Experiencing strong failure and loneliness when seeing happy couples
Avoiding socializing out of fear of being rejected

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Believes others will judge or reject oneself because of the divorce
Insisting 'they all think so' even without direct evidence

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently limiting oneself with 'I am unworthy of entering relationships'
Excessively worrying about being rejected before socializing, then withdrawing

exception_events.target_problem: When trying to interact or socialize with others, the client usually anticipates being judged and chooses avoidance, further intensifying loneliness.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In work settings, colleagues still respect him after learning of his divorce, have not changed their attitude toward him, and he maintains good professional interactions and relationships with colleagues.
exception_events.reason: Different supporting evidence: colleagues show respect based on professional competence; real experience shows not everyone evaluates negatively because of divorce.

positive_force: Has professional competence and gains colleagues' respect and support
Clear motivation to seek help, positive attitude, and willing to try changes (such as small social activities)
Able to identify and begin questioning negative beliefs (willingness for reality testing)
negative_force: Low sense of self-worth accompanied by self-denial
Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and mind reading
Fear of being rejected and being judged leading to social avoidance
Sleep disrupted, increased emotional burden affecting functioning

target_behavior.behavior: Social avoidance and fear of being rejected
antecedent: Trying to socialize with new people
target_behavior.core_reason: Viewing divorce as personal failure and catastrophically inferring the future, forming overgeneralized and mind-reading cognitions, triggering shame and fear of being rejected.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential judgment and rejection, reducing anxiety and shame in the short term.
target_behavior.consequence: Increased interpersonal isolation and loneliness, work performance affected, declining sleep quality.
